newsitem.title: USA: Republicans call Clinton meeting "very positive".
newsitem.headline: Republicans call Clinton meeting "very positive".

text.p: Top Republicans emerged from a meeting with President Bill Clinton on Tuesday saying they had had a "very positive" discussion, particularly on the topics of balancing the budget and reforming campaign finance.

"I thought we had a very positive meeting, looking at how we can solve problems next year. I think there's a real desire on the part of everybody to find a way to spend a year really working on solutions," said House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich, a Republican.
Republican Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott echoed Gingrich's assessment in talking to reporters.

"We were able to cooperate a great deal in the last two months of the last (congressional) session," Lott said. "Even with an election underway we produced a lot of really good legislation ... so we have a model of how to get the job done," he said, adding that he believes chances for passing a constitutional amendment to balance the budget have improved.
In the one sign of Republican caution, Lott suggested he would leave to Clinton the thorny task of proposing ways to reform the popular Medicare health care programme for the elderly.

"The president will need to make it clear that we have important and tough decisions we need to make in that area," Lott said. "When he lays out the problem and suggests a solution, we're certainly going to be prepared to work with him."
